subject: general
question: The Salal Project, also called the Salal Hydroelectric Power Station, is on which river?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chenab.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Salal Project, also known as the Salal Hydroelectric Power Station, is located on the **Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir, **India.
 
• The Chenab River originates in the Himalayas and flows approximately** 960 km through India and Pakistan**, and is one of the five rivers of Punjab, crucial for irrigation and agriculture.
 
• The project has a total installed capacity of** 690 MW,** generating electricity to meet regional demand.
 
• The Chenab also has major tributaries, including the **Jhelum and Ravi rivers,** contributing to its significance.
 
• The Salal Project plays a vital role in flood control and irrigation in addition to power generation, and it is managed by the **National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4b9e6b0700bcf754488b69efa41a79c2ad91fed704ecfb382a9d71f2577646b.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ravi:
 
 
• The Ravi River flows approximately **720 km** and is another important river in the region, flowing through India and Pakistan.
 
• It is** one of the five rivers of Punjab, and the Ranjit Sagar Dam **built on this river provides hydroelectric power and irrigation.
 
 
 
• Ganga:
 
 
• The Ganga River **originates from the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand** and flows for about **2,525 km** through northern India into Bangladesh.
 
• Considered sacred in Hinduism, the Ganga is vital for millions who depend on it for water and agriculture, and efforts like the** Ganga Action Plan** aim to address pollution and conserve the river.
 
 
 
• Krishna:
 
 
• The Krishna River originates in the **Western Ghats of Maharashtra **and flows approximately 1,400 km through Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• This river is crucial for irrigation and drinking water supply, with major projects like the **Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam dams **supporting its significance.
